The best free vector graphics editors

For logos, icons and illustrations you need a vector editor, and three good ones are free with no subscription: a mature desktop app, a browser app in Illustrator style and a new open source editor.

We make SlopVector, one of the tools on this page. Every fact about the other tools comes from their own pages, linked under each one, as they read on 2026-10-24. Prices and features change: check each site before you choose.

How we compared them

  • Free with no subscription or trial
  • Illustrator-style tools: pen, shapes, boolean operations, layers, text
  • Files in and out: SVG, PDF, PNG and .ai
  • Where it runs and how mature it is

1. Inkscape

Best for: Serious illustration work on the desktop, with the most complete free toolset and broad file support.

Good

  • Mature free and open source vector editor with SVG as its native format
  • Opens AI and PDF files; exports PDF, PNG, EPS and more
  • Boolean operations on paths and nested layers
  • Builds for Linux, macOS and Windows, including ARM64

Not so good

  • A desktop install, not a web page
  • No longer exports .ai files
  • PDF import approximates gradient meshes and drops transparency modes

Inkscape website · Sources: Inkscape home, Inkscape features, Inkscape 1.4.4 downloads, Inkscape for Illustrator users (wiki), Installing Inkscape (wiki)

2. SlopVector (ours)

Best for: Logos and icons in the browser, with Illustrator-style tools and nothing to install.

Good

  • Pen, shapes, type and layers with familiar shortcuts
  • Real pathfinder booleans
  • Exports SVG, PNG at 1×, 2× or 4×, JPG, PDF with vector paths, and a PDF-compatible .ai
  • Works on your device and offline; open source (MIT)

Not so good

  • Cannot open .ai or PDF files
  • SVG import ignores clip paths and skips linked images
  • No collaboration or cloud sync
  • Fewer tools than Inkscape

Open SlopVector

3. Graphite

Best for: Trying a new open source editor with node-based procedural design in the browser.

Good

  • Forever free and open source
  • Node-based procedural layers alongside vector editing
  • Runs locally in the browser with no server
  • Exports images at any size

Not so good

  • In alpha: more robust booleans, broader SVG support and PDF export are still planned
  • No .ai or PDF import yet; collaboration is planned
  • Raster editing is limited and experimental

Graphite website · Sources: Graphite home, Graphite features and roadmap, Graphite licence

Which one to choose

Inkscape comes first: it is the most complete free vector editor and opens .ai and PDF files, if you are happy to install it.

SlopVector is the one to use when you want to work in the browser with no install or account, and it can hand a PDF-compatible .ai to an Illustrator user. Graphite is promising and fully open source, but still in alpha.

Questions

What is the best free alternative to Illustrator?

Inkscape on the desktop, for the most features. In the browser, SlopVector has Illustrator-style tools and shortcuts and needs no install.

Can a free editor open .ai files?

Inkscape opens AI files (version 9 and later). SlopVector and Graphite cannot open them, though SlopVector can export a PDF-compatible .ai.

Which free vector editor runs in a browser?

SlopVector and Graphite. Inkscape is a desktop program for Linux, macOS and Windows.

Are they really free?

Yes. All three are free with no subscription, and all three are open source.
